title: Project Accounting Standards: Progress Installment Amount on Replacement System Installations
content:
# Progress installment amount

## Standard

The progress installment on a Replacement System Installations project is 30 percent of the project's net amount, which is every charge on the project less every credit on it, rounded to the cent half up.

## Terms used

- **Every charge on the project:** every charge entry on the project ledger — the contract-price charge, change-order charges, the permit-fee charge, labor-warranty upgrade charges, accessory charges and any other charge.
- **Every credit on the project:** every credit entry on the project ledger, of whatever kind.
- **Net amount:** the first total less the second. Payments on the project are neither charges nor credits and are not part of the net amount.

## Order of the computation

1. From the net amount, any amount excluded from the progress base and any charge collected in full are taken off, and the result is never below zero.
2. The progress share is applied once to what remains.
3. That amount is multiplied by its multiplier; a multiplier of 1 leaves it unchanged.
4. Charges collected in full are then added.
5. Only the final amount is rounded to the cent half up.

## Worked example (hypothetical project)

A hypothetical scheduled project carries a $9295.00 contract-price charge and a $112.00 permit-fee charge and no credits.

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Every charge on the project | $9407.00 |
| Every credit on the project | $0.00 |
| Net amount | $9407.00 |
| 30 percent of the net amount | $2822.10 |
| Progress installment, rounded to the cent | $2822.10 |

## Worked order (hypothetical stage values)

On a hypothetical net amount of $14000.00 with $5000.00 excluded from the progress base, a $600.00 charge collected in full, a 30 percent share and a multiplier of 0.95: $14000.00 less $5000.00 less $600.00 is $8400.00; 30 percent of it is $2520.00; multiplied by 0.95 it is $2394.00; adding the $600.00 gives $2994.00.
